new_entities.name: Live birth rate in diminished ovarian reserve
aliases: live birth success in women with DOR
IVF live birth in poor reserve
new_entities.description: Probability of live birth after IVF or ICSI among women with diminished ovarian reserve or poor ovarian response.

edges.effect_quant: The highest-signal takeaway is that DHEA has not convincingly increased live birth in randomized-only analyses. The 2023 Frontiers meta-analysis found no significant live birth increase when restricted to RCTs, and the 2023 systematic review found a live birth RR of 1.35 with confidence intervals crossing the null despite improvements in some intermediate IVF markers.
edges.population: women with diminished ovarian reserve or poor ovarian response undergoing IVF or ICSI
edges.mechanism: DHEA is proposed to augment the intra-ovarian androgen environment, potentially improving follicular recruitment and oocyte competence. The clinical problem is that plausible endocrine effects have not translated consistently into higher live birth rates in randomized evidence.
edges.summary: This is a classic mixed IVF adjunct edge. DHEA may improve some reserve markers or embryology metrics in selected women with diminished reserve, but the current randomized evidence does not justify a confident live-birth benefit claim.
edges.caveats: Definitions of diminished reserve and poor response vary across studies, and many meta-analyses pool RCTs with weaker observational designs. This edge should remain restrained and outcome-specific to live birth rather than being upgraded on the basis of intermediate markers alone.
